title: Andrew Carnegie, Three-Quarter Length Portrait
creator: Marceau, New York (photographer)
caption: Marceau's circa-1913 portrait of Andrew Carnegie — Gilded Age steel magnate and the figure whose 'Gospel of Wealth' defined the era's debate over industrial fortunes.
alt: Black-and-white three-quarter length studio portrait of an elderly Andrew Carnegie seated in a carved chair, facing slightly left of camera. He wears a dark three-piece suit with a white shirt and tie, his white beard neatly trimmed, and his hands rest on the arms of the chair. The background is a plain studio drape.
hostingInstitution: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division
rightsLabel: Public Domain — No Known Restrictions on Publication
citationChicago: Marceau, New York. [Andrew Carnegie, Three-Quarter Length Portrait, Seated, Facing Slightly Left]. Ca. 1913. Photograph. Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division, digital ID cph.3c01767. https://www.loc.gov/pictures/item/90715109/.

title: The Bosses of the Senate
creator: Joseph Keppler
caption: Joseph Keppler's January 23, 1889 Puck magazine cartoon showing industrial trusts as money-bag giants towering over tiny U.S. Senators — the Gilded Age's most famous indictment of corporate capture.
alt: Color political cartoon from 1889 depicting the U.S. Senate chamber dominated by enormous moneybag figures labeled STEEL, COPPER, OIL, IRON, SUGAR, TIN, COAL, and other industrial trusts. Tiny senators sit at desks below them. A door at the back marked PEOPLE'S ENTRANCE is bolted shut. A banner at top reads: This is the Senate of the Monopolists by the Monopolists and for the Monopolists.
hostingInstitution: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division
rightsLabel: Public Domain — No Known Restrictions on Publication
citationChicago: Keppler, Joseph. "The Bosses of the Senate." Puck, January 23, 1889. Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division, call number Illus. in AP101.P7 1889 (Case X). https://www.loc.gov/pictures/item/2002718861/.

title: Inspection Room, Ellis Island, New York
creator: Detroit Publishing Company
caption: A Detroit Publishing Company photograph of the inspection room at Ellis Island, where more than twelve million immigrants were processed between 1892 and 1954.
alt: Photograph of the interior of the Great Hall inspection room at Ellis Island, circa 1910 to 1920. American flags hang from the ceiling, tall windows line the walls, and rows of benches fill the cavernous space. The image shows the architectural scale of the federal immigration processing facility.
hostingInstitution: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division
rightsLabel: Public Domain — No Known Restrictions on Publication
citationChicago: Detroit Publishing Company. Inspection Room, Ellis Island, New York. Ca. 1910–1920. Photograph. Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division, Detroit Publishing Company photograph collection, digital ID LC-DIG-det-4a24564. https://www.loc.gov/pictures/item/2016812423/.

title: Five Cents a Spot — Unauthorized Immigrant Lodgings in a Bayard Street Tenement
creator: Jacob A. Riis
caption: Jacob Riis's 1889 flash photograph of a Bayard Street lodging house, published in How the Other Half Lives (1890) — the image that forced middle-class America to see tenement poverty.
alt: Black-and-white flash photograph from 1889 showing about a dozen poorly dressed men and women packed asleep on the floor and in bunks of a small, dimly lit tenement lodging room during a police raid. A metal pitcher and cookware sit on a ledge, and the walls are bare plaster lit by the photographer's flash.
hostingInstitution: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division
rightsLabel: Public Domain — No Known Restrictions on Publication
citationChicago: Riis, Jacob A. Five Cents a Spot — Unauthorized Immigrant Lodgings in a Bayard Street Tenement. 1889. Photograph. Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division, LOT 6300, digital ID cph 3a18572. https://www.loc.gov/pictures/item/2002710259/.

title: The Freedmen's Bureau
creator: Alfred R. Waud
caption: Alfred R. Waud's July 25, 1868 Harper's Weekly engraving of a Freedmen's Bureau officer standing between armed white and Black men — a visual argument for federal protection of newly freed Americans.
alt: Wood engraving cartoon from 1868 showing a central figure in Union Army uniform, representing the Freedmen's Bureau, standing with arms outstretched between an advancing mob of armed white men on the left and a group of armed African American men on the right. A United States flag flies from a building in the background. The title The Freedmen's Bureau appears at the bottom.
hostingInstitution: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division
rightsLabel: Public Domain — No Known Restrictions on Publication
citationChicago: Waud, Alfred R. "The Freedmen's Bureau." Harper's Weekly, July 25, 1868, 473. Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division, call number Illus. in AP2.H32 Case Y. https://www.loc.gov/pictures/item/92514996/.

title: Foreign Born Population, by States and Territories: 1890 (Statistical Atlas Diagram)
creator: Henry Gannett / U.S. Census Office
caption: Henry Gannett's 1898 Statistical Atlas diagram ranking states by foreign-born population in 1890 (New York leads with over 1.5 million) — the federal record of the 'Old Immigration' from Northern and Western Europe.
alt: Statistical Atlas page from 1898 titled Foreign Born Population by States and Territories 1890. A horizontal bar chart ranks states from most to fewest foreign-born residents, with New York, Pennsylvania, Illinois, and Massachusetts at the top. Explanatory text describes the distribution of foreign-born population by nationality and region.
hostingInstitution: Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division
citationChicago: Gannett, Henry, and U.S. Census Office. "Foreign Born Population, by States and Territories: 1890." In Statistical Atlas of the United States, Based upon the Results of the Eleventh Census. Washington, DC: U.S. Census Office, 1898. Library of Congress Geography and Map Division, call number G1201.G1 U53 1898. https://www.loc.gov/resource/g3701gm.gct00010/?sp=35.

title: Proportion of Wage Earners in Manufactures
creator: Henry Gannett / U.S. Census Office
caption: Henry Gannett's 1898 statistical map from the Eleventh Census showing the concentration of manufacturing wage earners in the Northeast and Midwest — a federal record of the Gilded Age industrial geography.
alt: Statistical choropleth map of the United States from 1898 titled Proportion of Wage Earners in Manufactures. States are shaded from light to dark based on the share of their workforce employed in manufacturing, with the Northeast and Great Lakes states in the darkest categories and the South and western territories in the lightest. A legend below the map lists the percentage brackets.
hostingInstitution: Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division
citationChicago: Gannett, Henry, and U.S. Census Office. "Proportion of Wage Earners in Manufactures." In Statistical Atlas of the United States, Based upon the Results of the Eleventh Census. Washington, DC: U.S. Census Office, 1898. Library of Congress Geography and Map Division, call number G1201.G1 U53 1898. https://www.loc.gov/resource/g3701gm.gct00010/?sp=86.

title: The Union As It Was — The Lost Cause, Worse Than Slavery (duplicate catalog record)
creator: Thomas Nast
caption: Alternate catalog scan of the October 24, 1874 Thomas Nast Harper's Weekly cartoon. Paired with nast-worse-than-slavery; preserved as a separate catalog entry because it is referenced by file name in the DOK question bank.
alt: Wood engraving political cartoon showing a hooded Ku Klux Klan member shaking hands with a figure labeled White League over a shield showing a terrified Black family cowering beneath a grinning skull labeled The Lost Cause. In the background a schoolhouse burns and an African American man hangs lynched from a tree. The caption reads: The Union as it was — The lost cause, worse than slavery.
hostingInstitution: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division
rightsLabel: Public Domain — No Known Restrictions on Publication
citationChicago: Nast, Thomas. "The Union as It Was — The Lost Cause, Worse Than Slavery." Harper's Weekly 18, no. 930 (October 24, 1874): 878. Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division. https://www.loc.gov/pictures/item/2001696840/.

title: The Union as It Was — The Lost Cause, Worse Than Slavery
creator: Thomas Nast
caption: Thomas Nast's October 24, 1874 Harper's Weekly cartoon indicting the Ku Klux Klan and White League for the terror campaign that ended Reconstruction.
alt: Wood engraving political cartoon showing a hooded Ku Klux Klan member shaking hands with a White League militiaman over a shield depicting an African American couple mourning their dead child. In the background, a schoolhouse burns and a lynched man hangs from a tree. The caption reads: The Union As It Was — The Lost Cause, Worse Than Slavery.
hostingInstitution: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division
rightsLabel: Public Domain — No Known Restrictions on Publication
citationChicago: Nast, Thomas. "The Union as It Was — The Lost Cause, Worse Than Slavery." Harper's Weekly, October 24, 1874. Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division, digital ID LC-USZ62-128619. https://www.loc.gov/pictures/item/2001696840/.

title: Radical Members of the First Legislature After the War, South Carolina
creator: Shorey (photographer)
caption: An 1876 photomontage of 63 members of South Carolina's first post-Civil War legislature — a majority-Black legislative body whose existence and dissolution frame the Reconstruction story.
alt: Photomontage composite on a card mount showing 63 individual bust portraits of members of the first post-Civil War South Carolina legislature. The portraits are arranged in eight rows, each identified by name beneath the image. The majority of the legislators pictured are African American.
hostingInstitution: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division
rightsLabel: Public Domain — No Known Restrictions on Publication
citationChicago: Shorey (photographer). Radical Members of the First Legislature After the War, South Carolina. Ca. 1876. Photomontage. Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division, digital ID LC-DIG-ppmsca-30572. https://www.loc.gov/pictures/item/97504690/.

title: Matthews, Northrup & Co's Official Railroad Map of the United States, Dominion of Canada and Mexico
creator: Matthews-Northrup Company
caption: An 1890 color railroad map showing the dense post-transcontinental rail network that knit the United States together by the end of Reconstruction.
alt: Color map of North America showing the dense U.S. railroad network in 1890. Solid lines mark completed tracks radiating from major eastern cities and reaching to the Pacific coast; dashed lines mark unfinished routes. Western states show sparser networks than the dense eastern grid. An inset at lower right details the railroads of Mexico.
hostingInstitution: Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division
rightsLabel: Public Domain — No Known Restrictions on Publication
citationChicago: Matthews, Northrup & Co. Matthews, Northrup & Co's Official Railroad Map of the United States, Dominion of Canada and Mexico Perfected to Date from Latest Authentic Sources. Buffalo, 1890. Map. Library of Congress Geography and Map Division, call number G3701.P3 1890 .M3. https://www.loc.gov/item/gm71000843/.

title: Sylvester Rawding Family in Front of Sod House, North of Sargent, Custer County, Nebraska
creator: Solomon D. Butcher
caption: Solomon Butcher's 1886 photograph of the Rawding family in front of their Nebraska sod house — a vivid record of Homestead Act settlement on the Great Plains.
alt: Black-and-white photograph from 1886 showing the Rawding family — Sylvester, Emma, and their four children — posed in front of their sod house in Custer County, Nebraska. A mule team stands to the right, a cow grazes on the grass-covered roof, and a table set with a watermelon sits in the foreground on the open prairie.
hostingInstitution: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division
rightsLabel: Public Domain — No Known Restrictions on Publication
citationChicago: Butcher, Solomon D. Sylvester Rawding Family in Front of Sod House, North of Sargent, Custer County, Nebraska. 1886. Photograph. Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division, LOT 3026, digital ID LC-DIG-ppmsca-08372. https://www.loc.gov/pictures/item/2005693378/.

title: Next!
creator: Udo J. Keppler
caption: Udo Keppler's September 7, 1904 Puck cartoon depicting Standard Oil as a giant octopus strangling American industry and reaching for the White House — the visual shorthand that launched Teddy Roosevelt's trust-busting.
alt: Color political cartoon from 1904 showing a giant octopus rising from a steel storage tank labeled STANDARD OIL. The octopus's tentacles wrap around a labeled state capitol, a U.S. Capitol, and buildings representing the steel, copper, and shipping industries. A fifth tentacle reaches toward the White House in the distance. The word Next! appears above the White House.
hostingInstitution: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division
rightsLabel: Public Domain — No Known Restrictions on Publication
citationChicago: Keppler, Udo J. "Next!" Puck 56, no. 1436 (September 7, 1904). Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division, digital ID LC-DIG-ppmsca-25884. https://www.loc.gov/pictures/item/2001695241/.

title: Tom Torlino, Navajo, Before and After
creator: John N. Choate
caption: J. N. Choate's before-and-after studio portraits of Navajo student Tom Torlino at the Carlisle Indian Industrial School — the most widely reproduced propaganda image of federal Indian assimilation policy.
alt: Side-by-side studio portraits of Navajo student Tom Torlino. On the left, Torlino in 1882 wears traditional Navajo clothing with long hair, large earrings, and a silver necklace. On the right, Torlino in 1885 wears a dark suit and white shirt with closely cropped hair, his skin appearing lighter due to the studio lighting. Both portraits are bust-length against a plain backdrop.
hostingInstitution: Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library, Yale University — Richard Henry Pratt Papers (WA MSS S-1174)
rightsLabel: Public Domain — U.S. Copyright Expired (pre-1929 publication)
citationChicago: Choate, John N. Tom Torlino, Navajo, Before and After. 1882 and 1885. Photographs. Richard Henry Pratt Papers (WA MSS S-1174), Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library, Yale University. Public-domain scan via Wikimedia Commons, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Tom_Torlino_Navajo_before_and_after_circa_1882.jpg.

title: Golden Spike Ceremony at Promontory, Utah
creator: Andrew J. Russell
caption: Andrew J. Russell's photograph of the Golden Spike Ceremony at Promontory Summit, Utah, May 10, 1869 — completion of the first transcontinental railroad.
alt: Photograph of Union Pacific locomotive 119 facing Central Pacific Jupiter at Promontory Summit, Utah, on May 10, 1869. Engineers shake hands between the two engines while a crowd of workers, officials, and onlookers celebrates the meeting of the rails.
citationChicago: Russell, Andrew J. Golden Spike Ceremony at Promontory, Utah. 1869. Photograph. National Archives and Records Administration, Record Group 16-G, item 99-1-1, Local Identifier 594940. https://catalog.archives.gov/id/594940.
